analysis.title: US Economic Notes: What you need to know for the week ahead
key_insights: DB expects the Fed to hike 25bps at each of its next three meetings, taking the fed funds rate to 4.625% by end of Q1 2027. The forecast was revised up after the stronger-than-expected October CPI report.

Chair Warsh speaks Monday at noon in San Francisco, moderating a panel where the first of his five task forces (productivity and jobs) presents findings. DB does not expect him to discuss the near-term policy outlook there.
Twelve other Fed officials appear this week. DB will watch them for changes in policy outlook after the October inflation data.
The October FOMC minutes are released Wednesday. DB calls them somewhat stale given the CPI data, but a useful benchmark for how policy views have evolved.

DB's baseline is that the AI task force focuses on AI lifting productivity and producing strong growth that may not be inflationary. It could also cover AI disruption of the US labor market and the effect on r-star.

Trump is expected to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. DB expects little new on US-China trade, where it expects the current détente to hold, or on Ukraine/Russia.

Tuesday's retail sales and industrial production reports are the main data highlights. DB forecasts headline retail sales unchanged (vs +0.8% prior) on lower auto sales, and retail control at +0.4% (vs +0.1%).
DB forecasts October industrial production at +0.2% (vs +0.7%) on lower utility output. Higher manufacturing hours worked in the October jobs report point to healthy factory activity.

Recent inflation data showed broad-based gains, reinforcing DB's concern about persistent price pressures. Labor data raise the risk that further tightening lets wages re-emerge as an inflation source.

Financial conditions have tightened in recent weeks. A reassessment of AI valuations has widened credit spreads and pushed equities lower. DB says this is not yet enough to replace the need for hikes, but a larger and longer move could give the Fed pause on quickening the pace of hikes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: DB projects 25bps hikes at each of the next three FOMC meetings.
Lower auto sales are expected to weigh on the headline.
Gasoline prices are expected to drag on sales excluding autos.
The series used to benchmark goods spending in GDP. DB expects it to point to healthy consumer demand growth.
Slower headline on utility output. Manufacturing hours worked point to healthy factory activity.

risk_factors: Further tightening could bring wages back as a source of inflationary pressure.
Further tightening of financial conditions from the AI valuation reassessment (wider credit spreads, lower equities) could give the Fed pause on quickening the pace of hikes.
Elevated geopolitical risks around the APEC meetings.
geopolitical: APEC summit: Trump expected to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines
US-China trade détente expected to be maintained
Ukraine/Russia conflict, which DB says has proven difficult for Trump to broker a peace agreement on

tension_points.theme: Fed hike pace vs tighter conditions
tension_points.bull_case: DB sees broad-based inflation gains and a labor market that could push wages up, so it expects 25bps hikes at each of the next three meetings.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter financial conditions from the AI valuation reassessment (wider credit spreads, falling equities) could make the Fed slow its pace of hikes if the moves extend in magnitude and duration.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An extension in magnitude and duration of the tightening in financial conditions (wider credit spreads, lower equities).

theme_stances.key_argument: Broad-based inflation gains and labor market strength mean financial tightening is not yet enough to replace rate hikes.
theme_stances.evidence: we revised up our expectations for Fed tightening
